Eli (sales): Flagging: HealthyLife POC is seeing intermittent JSON.parse errors when using streaming + function calls. UI shows "Unexpected end of JSON input". Non-streaming OK.
Eli (sales): They report it started after a load test, frontend opens multiple concurrent streams.
quota-bot: account_limit event for acct-healthylife at 1956789099 - burst_count=605 limit=600 - issuing 429s.
Eli (sales): Raw capture from their client (redacted):
```
chunk1: {"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_call":"{\"name\":\"normalize\",\"arguments\":{\"notes\":\"Partial start\"}\"}"}}]}
chunk2: {"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_call":"...middle content\"}}]}
chunk3: {"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_call":"...end but truncated}}"], "finish_reason": "stop"}
client error: JSON.parse failed: Unexpected end of JSON input
```
Nora (eng): Two likely causes: 1) mid-stream 429 closes connection leaving incomplete object; 2) our stream framing can split the tool_call JSON across several deltas with no explicit boundary token so naive parsers try to parse early.
Devon (solutions): Short-term recommendations to HealthyLife for the POC: a) cap frontend concurrency to <=4, b) add a robustness layer that accumulates chunks and only JSON.parse on a final marker or when finish_reason seen, c) implement a client fallback: if stream parsing fails after stream end, re-issue the same request with streaming=false.
Eli (sales): Customer asked if we can add a server-side safety net to avoid them having to change the UI for demos.
Kai (infra): I can temporarily raise their burst cap to 1200 for 72 hours and turn on tenant debug streaming logs. Doing that now.
Devon (solutions): Suggest emitting a structural end marker instead of a magic token (e.g., send a small metadata event: {"rwd_meta":{"seq":123,"final":true}}) so parsers can detect completion without exposing sentinel text to users. This avoids PII concerns.
Nora (eng): We have a tracking issue for stream assembler robustness. Plan: hold tool_call fragments in an assembler and only forward completed JSON objects to the stream layer. This avoids race where client parses mid-assembly. Creating ticket INF-3599. ETA: patch in next sprint.
QA-Zara: INF-3599 created and assigned to Nora. Repro steps: simulate parallel streams >6 and mid-stream abort (HTTP 429). Validate client fallback and server sanitizer behaviors.
Kai (infra): Burst cap increased at 1956789125. Monitoring shows 429s drop to zero for that tenant.
Eli (sales): Shared the cap bump + recommended client changes with HealthyLife. They implemented the buffered parser approach and reduced concurrency; streams now complete successfully.
Eli (sales): Closing the POC blocker for now; tracking INF-3599 for a permanent fix. Thanks team :raised_hands:
